Lessons.Title: Squares and Square Roots
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Comprehend that the symbol $\sqrt{x}$ denotes only the positive square root of $x$. Explain why equations of the form $x^2 = a$ can have two solutions, while equations of the form $\sqrt{x} = a$ cannot have more than one solution.
sqrt(x) for x>=0 is nonnegative, but x^2=a>0 has two real solutions. Do not automatically add ± to the radical symbol.

Source activity 6.1: Math Talk: Four Squares: Find the solutions of each equation mentally. \(x^2 = \text{-}1\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 6.2: Finding Square Roots: Clare was adding \(\sqrt{4}\) and \(\sqrt{9}\), and at first she wrote \(\sqrt{4} + \sqrt{9} = 2+3\). But then she remembered that 2 and -2 both square to make 4, and that 3 and -3 both square to make 9. She wrote down all the possible combinations: 2 + 3 = 5 2 + (-3) = -1 (-2) + 3 = 1 (-2) + (-3) = -5 Then she wondered, “Which of these are the same as \(\sqrt{4} + \sqrt{9}\)?… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 6.3: One Solution or Two?: The graph of \(b=\sqrt{a}\) is shown. Complete the table with the exact values and label the corresponding points on the graph with the exact values. Label the point on the graph that shows the solution to \(\sqrt{a} = 4\). Label the point on the graph that shows the solution to \(\sqrt{a} = 5\). Label the point on the graph that shows the solution to \(\sqrt{a} = \sqrt{5}\).… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
Practice Problem 1: Select all solutions to the equation \(x^2=7\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: Find the solution(s) to each equation, if there are any. \(\sqrt{x}=\text-3\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: If \(c\) is a positive number, how many solutions does \(x^2=c\) have? Explain. If \(c\) is a positive number, how many solutions does \(\sqrt{x}=c\) have? Explain. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Suppose that a friend missed class and never learned what \(37^{\frac13}\) means. Use exponent rules your friend would already know to calculate \((37^{\frac13})^3\). Explain why this means that \(37^{\frac13}\) is the cube root of 37. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 5: Evaluate \(8^{\frac53}\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Write each expression without using exponents. \(4^{\text-\frac32}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Solve u^2=36 and sqrt(v)=6. Expected reasoning or answer: u=±6; v=36.
